method: Read-only current-source control-flow audit. Findings are source-confirmed paths, not native reproductions. No runtime pass is asserted.

findings.title: Note-list read failure is presented as an empty list
findings.severity: S3: notes query failure is indistinguishable from a genuinely empty collection
findings.priority: P1: user cannot tell whether their notes are absent or the read failed
reproduction: Open Notes while signed in with the selected device organization set.
Make the notes SELECT return a Supabase error (for example, deny the read or make the network unavailable).
Observe Notes after the query settles.
findings.expected: The query failure is visibly distinct from a successful empty result, with an available recovery action or clear retry guidance.
findings.actual: listMyNotes logs the error and returns []; NotesView receives a successful query result and renders NotesList, which says ‘No notes yet’ with no error state.
findings.next_fix: Preserve the read failure as an error result (rather than empty data), render an explicit error state in NotesView, and provide retry/reopen guidance.

findings.title: Failed note creation produces no user-visible result
findings.severity: S3: create failure is silent in the Notes surface
findings.priority: P2: user repeats the action or assumes a note was created
reproduction: Open Notes as a signed-in user with organization selected.
Make the notes INSERT fail, such as by denying it at the database boundary.
Click New note and observe the settled UI.
findings.expected: The failed create is reported and the user remains in the list with a clear way to retry.
findings.actual: createNote converts a database error into null; NotesList only changes selection when the result is truthy and renders no error or notice for null.
findings.next_fix: Return a surfaced failure from createNote and display an actionable error beside the create control; preserve creating cleanup.

findings.title: Debounced note edits are dropped when a save is already in flight
findings.severity: S2: latest user edits can be lost while the UI reports an earlier snapshot saved
reproduction: Open a note and change its body; allow the 600 ms debounce to start the update request.
Before that request resolves, make a second body change and wait for its 600 ms debounce to expire.
Let the first request succeed, then reload the note.
findings.expected: The latest draft is eventually persisted, and ‘Saved’ refers to that latest draft.
findings.actual: The second timer calls persist while inflightRef is true; persist returns immediately and discards that snapshot. Completion of the first update marks the earlier snapshot saved and does not schedule a trailing write.
findings.next_fix: Serialize writes while retaining the newest queued draft; after each in-flight write settles, persist the latest draft if it differs from the saved snapshot.

findings.title: Files read failure also renders an empty-library or empty-captures claim
findings.severity: S3: an error is accompanied by a contradictory empty-state claim
findings.priority: P2: user may infer files or screenshots do not exist
reproduction: Open Files as a signed-in user with the selected organization set and no cached rows.
Inspect the active Library or Screenshots tab after loading ends.
findings.expected: Show the read error and retry state without describing the collection as empty.
findings.actual: reload sets state to error and displays the error banner, but both tab panels branch only on state === loading and then use an empty-row test; the active panel additionally says ‘No library files yet’ or ‘No captures yet’.
findings.next_fix: Render explicit error/retry content in the active tab before its empty-state branch; distinguish successful empty reads from failed reads.

findings.title: Concurrent saved-capture opens can select a different item than the last click
findings.severity: S3: delayed detail response can navigate to a stale capture
findings.priority: P2: user sees the wrong saved Source after selecting another row
reproduction: From a list with two Sources, click Source A, then click Source B before A’s getSavedCapture request returns.
Arrange for B’s request to return first and A’s request to return last.
Observe the detail selected after both requests complete.
findings.expected: The detail view corresponds to the most recent row selection, Source B.
findings.actual: openCapture has no request generation or selected-ID guard; each resolution calls setSelected, so the slower A response overwrites B.
findings.next_fix: Guard detail-open results with a monotonically increasing request generation or current selected ID so stale responses cannot replace the latest selection.

coverage_limits: No browser, live data, build, or test execution was performed; the listed triggers are derived from concrete current-source branches and need native verification before closure.
No additional defects are claimed for the remaining controls in EXT-F-2006 through EXT-F-2009; their behavior was not exhaustively runtime exercised.
